title: Phishing, Social Engineering and Impersonation
summary: How attackers manipulate people through email, phone, text, messaging apps and fake websites, including AI-generated voices and video, and the habits that stop them.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How attackers manipulate people through email, phone, text, messaging apps and fake websites, including AI-generated voices and video, and the habits that stop them.
Learning Objectives: Recognise the signs of phishing, vishing, smishing and business email compromise
Identify deepfake and other AI-enabled impersonation attempts
Apply verification steps before acting on unusual or urgent requests
Syllabus: Phishing, vishing, smishing and QR-code attacks
Business email compromise and payment diversion
Deepfake voices and video: impersonating executives and customers
Pause, verify, report: call-back and dual-control habits
Intended Audience: All staff in regulated firms, including new joiners, contractors and temporary staff with access to the firm's systems
Front-office, operations, technology, HR, finance and support staff who handle customer data or critical processes
Line managers responsible for secure working practices and continuity arrangements in their teams
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No technical background is required. The programme is suitable for new joiners and as annual refresher training.
Core Reading: ISO/IEC (2022), ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Information Security, Cybersecurity and Privacy Protection – Information Security Management Systems – Requirements
ISO (2019), ISO 22301:2019 Security and Resilience – Business Continuity Management Systems – Requirements
